acceptance_criteria.statement: ExecuteApprovedProposal runs current Workspace/resource authorization, ExecutionAuthorizer and exact compatibility before acquisition and again after AcquireApplied immediately before dispatch authorization. Denial records before_provider_receive, makes zero gateway calls, remains executing and returns 202 without blind retry authority.
Exact m4r1 integrity/key/expiry/Workspace/capability/binding is verified at both current checkpoints; every denial produces zero gateway calls.
Logical execution identity and canonical-json-v1 fingerprint over the complete exact provider intent are server-derived, immutable and never client input.

acquire_execution captures PostgreSQL transaction_timestamp once and atomically creates generation 1 with lease_started_at and lease_expires_at equal to database time plus bounded duration. Application time never determines lease creation or expiry.
Concurrent acquisition has exactly one applied generation-1 winner; all losers are typed and make zero gateway calls.

After the second current check, authorize_execution_dispatch revalidates current owner, exact generation and unexpired deadline using PostgreSQL time and returns an opaque integrity-protected m4-dispatch-v1 permit. Fencing before permit issuance makes zero gateway calls; the provider verifies permit identity/integrity/deadline before any SQLite write, so a stale/expired generation cannot create the external side effect.

SQLite atomically commits external ticket/rejection plus authoritative idempotency fingerprint/outcome in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Same fingerprint replays, different fingerprint conflicts and before/after-commit faults cannot duplicate the side effect.
Only direct success and the three closed target_not_found, validation_rejected and policy_rejected outcomes finalize succeeded/failed with sanitized mapping.

Receipt-possible outcomes are executing/202. Provider fingerprint conflict is executing/409 TOOL_PROVIDER_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT with sanitized audit and no retry. Invalid/expired dispatch permit proves no write, records before_provider_receive and remains executing/202 for Issue #78 provider-first recovery.

Both authorization decisions, compatibility, PostgreSQL-time lease/permit, provider identity, immutable intent, observations and outcome reconstruct from append-only audit while M1-M3 regressions remain green.

design_decisions.decision: Current authorization and compatibility are checked before acquisition and at the last barrier before PostgreSQL-authorized provider dispatch.
authorize_execution_dispatch is the generation-1 dispatch fence; it uses database time and mints a domain-separated permit binding exact lease and approved intent.

The provider verifies the permit before its atomic SQLite effect/idempotency transaction. Since takeover is legal only after the prior database deadline, the old permit is expired before a higher-generation dispatch can be issued.
Indeterminate receipt, permit rejection and fingerprint conflict remain non-terminal observations with explicit 202/409 mappings; only closed provider outcomes finalize.
Issue #77 owns generation-1 acquire/dispatch/fencing. Issue #78 owns takeover, generation 2+, reconciliation and post-takeover finalization proof.

invariants: No provider dispatch without both current authority/compatibility checkpoints and a current PostgreSQL-authorized permit.
m4-dispatch-v1 permits are integrity-protected, purpose-bound, immutable and never request input.
The provider validates permit deadline before any external/idempotency mutation.
PostgreSQL transaction time alone creates and evaluates leases; process-clock skew is irrelevant.
Provider effect and idempotency outcome commit atomically or both roll back.
Fingerprint conflict never becomes terminal or grants retry authority.
Capability registry remains static/typed; no plugin framework, model/system approval or raw provider data exposure.
out_of_scope: ReconcileExecution, stale-lease takeover, generation 2+ and post-takeover finalization, owned by Issue #78.
Vendor production integration, dynamic plugins or capability discovery.
Editing immutable proposals or reusing approval after material capability/binding/policy change.
